package_info.package_manager: source (C++ library, used in OpenSAML/Shibboleth, distributed via Linux repos and bundled in proprietary products)
package_info.why_malicious: The xmltooling package contains a critical Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability (CVE-2023-36661) that allows attackers to supply malicious XML input. When the library parses this input, it can resolve attacker-controlled URIs specified in KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements, leading to unauthorized network requests. This can be exploited to access internal resources, perform denial of service, or facilitate unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability is present by default in all affected versions and can be triggered without authentication, making these versions highly dangerous in any security-sensitive deployment.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the xmltooling library parses XML input, such as during SAML authentication or metadata processing)
execution_context.file_location: core xmltooling library code (C++), specifically in the XML parsing logic handling KeyInfo and RetrievalMethod elements
required_permissions: filesystem (if the URI points to a file resource or if the library writes fetched data to disk)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This XML snippet, when processed by vulnerable versions of xmltooling, causes the library to fetch and process the external URI specified in the RetrievalMethod. If the URI is attacker-controlled, it can be used to trigger SSRF, access internal resources, or deliver further payloads. The library does not restrict or validate the URI, allowing attackers to control the destination of the network request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing untrusted XML input to specify arbitrary external URIs for resolution enables attackers to force the application to make network requests to attacker-controlled or internal systems. This violates network trust boundaries and can be leveraged for SSRF, data exfiltration, or further exploitation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal SAML/XML processing should only allow retrieval of keys or metadata from trusted, validated, or whitelisted sources. Accepting and resolving arbitrary URIs from unauthenticated input is a severe security violation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate SAML implementations may use RetrievalMethod to fetch trusted keys or metadata, but only from pre-approved, whitelisted, or cryptographically validated sources. Unrestricted use is never safe.
key_indicators: Unrestricted resolution of URIs in KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements from untrusted XML input
Absence of URI validation or whitelisting in the XML parsing logic
Network requests initiated by the library in response to attacker-supplied XML
Ability to specify internal or external network locations in XML input

attack_chain.action: Attacker submits crafted SAML/XML input containing a KeyInfo element with a RetrievalMethod URI pointing to an attacker-controlled or internal resource.
attack_chain.leads_to: The vulnerable xmltooling library processes the XML and attempts to resolve the URI specified in the RetrievalMethod element.

attack_chain.action: The library makes a network request to the specified URI, potentially accessing internal services or fetching attacker-controlled data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can use SSRF to access restricted resources, exfiltrate data, or chain with other vulnerabilities (e.g., command injection) for further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests originating from SAML or XML processing services, especially during authentication or metadata parsing
Resolution of external URIs specified in KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements of XML input, particularly when the source is untrusted or unauthenticated
Network requests to internal IP addresses or sensitive endpoints (e.g., cloud metadata services) triggered by XML parsing processes
file_indicators: Presence of unpatched xmltooling library versions (<3.2.4) on the system
SAML/XML processing logs showing access to external or non-whitelisted URIs in KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements
Configuration files or deployment manifests referencing vulnerable xmltooling versions
network_indicators: Outbound requests to attacker-controlled domains or IPs from SAML processing hosts
Requests to internal network resources (e.g., 169.254.169.254, localhost, internal subnets) initiated by SAML/XML parsing processes
Unusual egress traffic patterns from authentication gateways or identity providers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor SAML and XML processing services for outbound network requests, especially those occurring during authentication or metadata parsing. Inspect application and security logs for KeyInfo/RetrievalMethod elements referencing external or non-whitelisted URIs. Use file integrity monitoring and software inventory tools to identify unpatched xmltooling library versions. Implement network egress controls to block unauthorized outbound requests from authentication gateways, and review for signs of SSRF exploitation such as access to internal or cloud metadata endpoints.
